title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

findings.explanation: The base code at lines 2115 and 2121 in src/documents/views.py was fetching MailRule and MailAccount objects without any ownership filtering. The code used `MailRule.objects.filter(name__icontains=query)` and `MailAccount.objects.filter(name__icontains=query)`, which returns ALL matching objects regardless of owner. The PR changes this to use `get_objects_for_user_owner_aware()`, which correctly implements owner-aware access control per the security policy. This is a fix for an IDOR vulnerability, not a new flaw. Since the PR removes the vulnerability from changed lines, this represents a security improvement and no authorization flaw in the PR itself.
findings.suggested_fix: N/A - This PR fixes a pre-existing vulnerability
